name: Hubbell Trading Post National Historic Site
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Hubbell Trading Post National Historic Site near Ganado, Arizona, preserves the oldest continuously operating trading post on the Navajo Nation. Established by John Lorenzo Hubbell in 1878, the post served as a vital center of commerce and cultural exchange between the Navajo people and the wider American economy. Hubbell became a trusted figure in the community, acting as interpreter, mediator, and advisor while building a business around Navajo weavings, silverwork, and other crafts. The trading post was designated a national historic site in 1965 and still functions as a working trading post today, selling Navajo rugs, jewelry, and pottery. The site preserves the Hubbell family home, a visitor center with historic rug collections, and the surrounding cultural landscape.
